claim: On the transient class Z, the chain jumps from i to i+1 and i-1 at rate one each and jumps to a separate absorbing cemetery at rate kappa+v*1_{i=0}, with kappa>0 and v>0. Its transient generator is Delta-kappa I-v|0><0|, where Delta f(i)=f(i+1)+f(i-1)-2f(i).

For the two-ended killed walk just defined, lambda=kappa, the class is lambda-transient, and for fixed integers i,j the limit of t^(3/2)*exp(kappa*t)*p_t(i,j) is [max(ij,0)+(|i|+|j|)/v+2/v^2]/(2*sqrt(pi)). This strictly positive kernel has rank two and its {0,1} minor is 1/(4*pi*v^2). It cannot factor as a rank-one product. This rechecks an existing campaign candidate and does not certify novelty.
assumptions: extra killing v>0 at lattice zero

claim: The supplied campaign already contains a candidate refutation of the rank-one polynomial-limit assertion for a lambda-transient killed chain. claim: For finite E and orthogonal unit vectors u,v in C^E, the projection law on span(u) chooses singleton {i} with mass |u_i|^2. The law on span(u,v) chooses {i,j}, i<j, with mass |u_i*v_j-u_j*v_i|^2. These are fixed-cardinality determinantal projection laws.
assumptions: u and v orthogonal unit vectors

claim: For finite E and orthogonal unit vectors u,v in C^E, there is a coupling of singleton projection laws on span(u) and span(v) whose disjoint union has projection law on span(u,v). A capacitated flow splits edge masses q_ij=|u_i*v_j-u_j*v_i|^2 between endpoints with first marginal |u_i|^2. Every required cut holds because its internal mass is U_A*V_A-|c_A|^2<=U_A, where U_A=sum_A|u_i|^2, V_A=sum_A|v_i|^2 and c_A=sum_A u_i*conjugate(v_i).
assumptions: u and v orthogonal unit vectors

claim: If H=H_1 orthogonal-sum H_2 on a finite ground set and one summand has rank one, the union-marginal coupling exists. Couple the other summand as a subset of a sample from P_H using projection stochastic domination and Strassen. The set difference is a singleton with inclusion masses equal to the rank-one projection diagonal, hence has exactly that summand law. This is a consequence of Lyons (2014), Theorem 2.7.

Finite evidence for the general union-marginal coupling question: eight rational orthogonal-matrix instances with summand ranks (2,2), four each in dimensions five and six, admit nonnegative rational coupling masses with all three determinantal marginals exactly correct. All eight saved points were independently replayed using Gram determinants. A float LP supplied only a support; exact arithmetic certified the points. These examples do not prove the general question.
assumptions: the eight matrices and rational masses in measurements/C0034_higher_rank_certificates.jsonl

claim: Sampling a rank-two projection pair C, choosing a singleton i in C with probability proportional to |u_i|^2, and giving the remaining endpoint to the second marginal need not reproduce either intended rank-one law. The saved rational three-coordinate counterexample has second-marginal total variation about 0.1136890368; the exact fraction and vectors are preserved. This refutes this splitting rule, not existence of another coupling.

Lyons arXiv:1406.2707 (2014), Question 2.8, asks whether orthogonal projection laws can be coupled with their union having the summed projection law. The supplied caches give no later general disposition. This packet proves rank-one-summand special cases and supplies eight exact higher-rank examples; the general question remains unresolved here.
assumptions: only the supplied local caches and prior records were consulted

claim: If an automorphism-equivariant factor-of-i.i.d. independent set on the d-regular tree has root density a>0, every b in [0,a] is also attainable by independently retaining its vertices with probability b/a, using an independent label family obtained by splitting the i.i.d. labels. If A is the supremum of attainable densities, the attainable set contains [0,A) and is contained in [0,A]; inclusion of A requires an attainment argument.
assumptions: automorphism-equivariant factor of independent uniform labels

claim: Suppose for every sufficiently large d the factor-of-i.i.d. density supremum on the d-regular tree is at most (5/4)*log(d)/d, while random d-regular graphs admit asymptotic independent-set density at least (7/4)*log(d)/d. Then the two attainable-density sets differ for those d. The cited Rahman-Virag and Ding-Sly-Sun asymptotics are a local literature lead; their primary statements were not reverified here.

Pete Conjecture 14.16 historically asks whether independent-set densities on random d-regular graphs equal factor-of-i.i.d. independent-set densities on the d-regular tree. The supplied ranking and C0151-A001 record a large-d refutation attributed to Rahman-Virag and Ding-Sly-Sun, but those primary answer papers were not verified here. The thinning endpoint correction is independently proved; current literature classification stays a lead pending source review.
assumptions: only the supplied local caches and prior records were consulted

claim: The n-vertex lattice trees in Z containing zero are exactly the n intervals [-L,n-1-L], L=0,...,n-1. Uniform L gives exact uniform rooted sampling using expected O(log n) unbiased random bits and a compact O(log n)-bit endpoint representation. Listing vertices takes O(n) word operations on an O(log n)-bit word RAM and O(n log n) bits of coordinate output. Trees modulo translation instead have one class.
assumptions: word RAM for the stated word-operation bound

claim: On Z^d, d>=1, grow a rooted tree from the origin by choosing uniformly from available boundary edges at each step. At three vertices the resulting distribution has total variation exactly 1/6 from the uniform rooted lattice-tree law. With D=2d there are 2D(D-1) equiprobable growth histories, but center-rooted trees have two histories and endpoint-rooted trees have one. This obstruction concerns this uncorrected growth rule.

Schramm (2006v2), Problem 2.9, asks for efficient approximate uniform sampling of n-vertex lattice trees containing the origin. The supplied prior attempt only gives inefficient enumeration. This packet solves the line special case and disproves uncorrected uniform frontier growth; general higher-dimensional status is unresolved from the supplied caches.
assumptions: only the supplied local caches and prior records were consulted

claim: Give each edge of K_n one independent identically distributed continuous weight and retain it if both endpoints rank it among their single lowest incident weights. For n>=2 the graph is a matching, a fixed edge is present with probability 1/(2n-3), and a fixed vertex is isolated with probability (n-2)/(2n-3). The expected number of isolates is n(n-2)/(2n-3); connectivity is impossible for n>2.
assumptions: one shared i.i.d. continuous weight per undirected edge

claim: In the same shared-weight bilateral model with n=6 and k=2, the event that all six edges inside two vertex triples precede all nine cross edges produces two disjoint triangles. It has probability 1/binomial(15,6)=1/5005, yet minimum degree is two. Thus absence of isolates is not a deterministic connectivity criterion. This finite event does not settle the asymptotic fine window.

Dabirian-Subramanian (cached 2025 version) establish a first-order logarithmic connectivity threshold for shared-weight bilateral preference graphs, while their introductory Open Problems leave a finer window. The supplied cache contains no later answer. The finite calibrations here establish no window width or limiting connectivity law.
assumptions: only the supplied local caches and prior records were consulted

claim: For independent Bernoulli(p) site colours, 0<p<1, boundary incidence patterns [a,b,a,c] and [a,b,c,d] both initially have colour word UUUU but induce different occurrence-colour laws. After exposing occurrence zero as black, occurrence two is black with probability 1 in the first pattern and p in the second. The full-law total variation is 2p(1-p). Thus the word alone cannot determine transitions uniformly conditional on each full boundary configuration. Retain incidence identities or supply a valid averaging/lumping theorem; no impossibility of weak lumping for a particular process is asserted.
assumptions: configurationwise transition rule, without a proved averaging theorem

claim: The prior claim that a Markov description of site-percolation peeling exists exactly for bounded face degrees is unsupported. Unbounded finite faces expose finitely many labels per step and allow larger states; bounded face degrees alone do not bound the accumulated boundary length. The proven correction here is only that nonsimple boundaries require vertex-identity information in addition to a colour word. No threshold or sufficient compressed state is established.
assumptions: finite degrees at each exposed face

claim: Let D=2d. Unoriented simple cycles through a fixed vertex in Z^d have square count 4*binomial(d,2) and six-cycle count 12*binomial(d,2)+96*binomial(d,3). In Q_D the corresponding counts are binomial(D,2) and 12*binomial(D,3). Thus lattice-minus-cube differences are -D/2 for squares and -(9/2)D(D-2) for six-cycles. The graphs are compared at the same degree, not the same dimension.

Lattice two-axis rectangles are absent from a hypercube, but at equal degree the hypercube has more total six-cycles. Therefore a comparison that counts only the extra lattice rectangles omits other subleading cycle-count changes. These exact counts do not identify the first distinct coefficient of the critical-probability expansions: lace-diagram weights, cancellation and the cube critical-parameter convention still require analysis. The earlier a_4 prediction remains a heuristic.

Heydenreich-van der Hofstad, Open Problem 15.9, asks for the first difference between lattice and cube critical-probability expansion coefficients after the first three agree. Exact short-cycle counts here correct an earlier heuristic but do not determine that index; later literature status is unverified.

claim: Orient a diamond as 0->a,b->c and let simple random walk use its underlying undirected unit-edge graph. Its probability of returning to 0 at two steps is 1/2, although a forward-only walk has return probability zero. Thus bond orientation in oriented percolation does not justify forbidding backward steps in the undirected random-walk spectral-dimension problem.
assumptions: simple random walk uses the underlying undirected cluster

claim: In a finite unit-conductance network between an origin and a target boundary, if m distinct singleton edge cuts separate them, effective resistance is at least m. Every unit flow has current of magnitude one through each cut edge, so its energy is at least m. More generally pairwise edge-disjoint separating cutsets C_j give the lower bound sum_j 1/|C_j|. This alone provides no random IIC bottleneck tail estimate.
assumptions: origin separated from wired target boundary

claim: For a simple undirected circulant graph on Z/nZ, let S contain one representative of each included unordered nonzero generator pair and m=floor(n/2). Its Lovasz theta number is n times the maximum z_0 subject to z_j>=0, sum_{j=0}^m z_j=1, and sum_{j=0}^m z_j*cos(2*pi*j*s/n)=0 for every s in S. Paired Fourier frequencies are aggregated; the zero and even-n self-inverse frequency remain unpaired. This is a rederivation of the LP already described in the cached 2025 source.

Include every unordered nonzero generator pair of Z/nZ independently with probability 1/2. Expected Lovasz theta is 3/2 for n=2, 2 for n=3, 9/4 for n=4, and (3+sqrt(5))/2 for n=5. At n=4 the four theta values are 4,2,2,1; at n=5 they are 5,sqrt(5),sqrt(5),1. These finite values do not establish the conjectured large-n asymptotic.
assumptions: fair independent inclusion of unordered nonzero generator pairs

claim: For fair random circulants on n vertices set Z=log(theta(G)/sqrt(n)). Vertex transitivity and complement symmetry give E theta(G)/sqrt(n)=E cosh(Z)>=1+E[Z^2]/2. Hence asymptotic expectation ratio one requires E[Z^2]->0. If also E exp(Z)<=exp(sigma_n^2/2) with sigma_n->0, that expectation ratio tends to one. The latter MGF bound is a sufficient hypothesis, not a bound proved for the random graph here.
assumptions: MGF hypothesis for the sufficient direction only

claim: Double-precision Fourier LP enumeration for all 60 fair-generator configurations on n=2,...,9 agrees with the exact n=2,...,5 expectations. Maximum equality residual was 1.1102230246251565e-15 and maximum theta-complement product discrepancy was 8.881784197001252e-15. These are numerical solver checks, not rational feasibility certificates and not proof of a large-n limit.
assumptions: the saved n=2,...,9 floating-point LP outputs

claim: For Bernoulli initial infection probability p on the four-regular tree, two-neighbor bootstrap has complete occupation almost surely for p>1/9 and fails almost surely for p<=1/9. Thus the complete-occupation critical infimum is 1/9. At p=1/9 the probability a specified root remains vacant is 21/32. Directed vacancy messages converge to the largest solution x=q(3x^2-2x^3), q=1-p; the critical largest solution is x=3/4 at q=8/9. This is a tree special case, not the general group characterization.
assumptions: complete occupation on the infinite graph

claim: Two-neighbor bootstrap on the three-regular tree completes almost surely at its critical infimum p=1/2, whereas on the four-regular tree it fails at its critical infimum p=1/9. The latter has positive critical residual vacancy 21/32 at the root. A critical threshold specified as an infimum therefore does not automatically assert occupation at the threshold itself.
assumptions: the three- and four-regular tree Bernoulli models
